[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard governs how enterprise AI agents connect to and interact with external systems. It establishes mandatory requirements for connection declaration, identity and authentication, operation classification, human-in-the-loop controls for consequential actions, credential management, and connection failure behavior. It applies to any agent that connects to a system beyond its native platform.
page_texts.5:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#scope]

### Scope

This standard applies to all AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents that connect to any external system — APIs, databases, internal services, SaaS platforms, messaging systems, or any other integration target — at Pilot and Production lifecycle states. It applies regardless of whether the connection is read-only or involves write or action operations.

This standard does not govern the access controls of the target systems themselves — those are governed by data governance and security standards. It governs the agent's declared connection, the identity model used, the permitted operations, and the controls applied before those operations execute.
page_texts.6:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

Mandatory. Any agent with one or more external system connections must have a complete System Connection Register before promotion to Pilot state.
page_texts.7:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Ungoverned agent connections to external systems are the most direct path to unintended data exposure, unauthorized state changes, and unauditable agent behavior. An agent that reads from or writes to a system it has not declared — under an identity it has not documented — operating without human review of consequential actions — is a governance failure regardless of how well its outputs are structured. This standard closes that gap for all agent types.

page_texts.9:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**Connection Declaration:**

Every external system connection used by an agent must be declared in the agent's System Connection Register before Pilot promotion. Each declared connection must include:

- System name and type — the name of the target system and whether it is a read data source, a write target, or an action/trigger endpoint
- Connection classification — one of: Read, Write, or Action (defined below)
- Identity model — the authentication identity the agent uses to access the system (User Delegated, Service Identity)
- Permitted operations — the explicit list of operations the agent is authorized to perform; operations not listed are prohibited
- Data sensitivity classification — the sensitivity level of the data accessed, modified, or triggered through this connection
- System owner — the named individual or team responsible for the target system's access governance
- Connection failure behavior — the agent's defined response when the system is unavailable
- Execution mode — Manual (human confirmation required before each operation) or Automated (approved for autonomous execution per the human-in-the-loop requirements below); required for Write and Action connections
- Credential rotation cadence — the documented schedule for rotating each service credential; required for Service Identity connections

Agents must not connect to any system not declared in the System Connection Register.

**Connection Classification:**

Every declared connection must be classified as one of:

- **Read** — the agent retrieves data from the system; no state change occurs in the target system as a result of the agent's operation
- **Write** — the agent creates, modifies, or deletes records in the target system. Record-level creates, updates, and deletes are classified as Write regardless of any resulting side-effect state change.
- **Action** — the agent initiates a process, workflow, event, or state change in the target system that is **not a direct record CRUD operation** (e.g., sending a message, triggering a pipeline, transitioning a workflow state). Record-level creates, updates, and deletes are classified as Write regardless of any resulting side-effect state change.

Write and Action connections carry higher governance requirements than Read connections.

**Identity and Authentication:**

Agents must use one of two permitted identity models:

- **User Delegated** — the agent operates under the identity of the authenticated user; the agent's access to the target system is bounded by the user's own permissions. This is the default and preferred model for Read connections.
- **Service Identity** — the agent uses a dedicated service account or managed identity to access the target system. This model is required when the agent must access a system on behalf of multiple users or independently of any user session. Service identities require written approval from both the Data and Compliance Owner and the target-system technical owner before provisioning, and must be scoped to the minimum permissions required for the declared permitted operations. Service identities must use managed identities or certificate-based authentication where the target system supports these mechanisms; static passwords and long-lived API keys must not be used for service identities.

Agents must not use a connection model that grants the agent access to data or operations the user would not have under the User Delegated model without documented justification and Data and Compliance Owner approval.

**Human-in-the-Loop for Write and Action Connections:**

Write and Action connections require a defined human review checkpoint before execution unless all three of the following conditions are met:

1. The capability contract explicitly documents the business justification for automated execution without human review
2. The Data and Compliance Owner has approved automated execution in writing
3. Audit logging is implemented for every autonomous execution — recording the operation type, system target, a redacted summary of operation parameters (excluding credentials, tokens, and sensitive payload data), timestamp, and outcome — and retained in a centrally accessible, tamper-resistant log

Where a human checkpoint is required, the agent must present the proposed write or action to the user for explicit confirmation before executing. The agent must not execute a write or action operation without receiving confirmation.

**Credential Management:**

- API keys, tokens, passwords, and other credentials used by agent connections must be stored in an approved secrets management service
- Credentials must not be embedded in prompts, system instructions, code, or configuration files that are not secret-managed
- The rotation cadence for each service credential must be documented in the System Connection Register
- Credentials must be scoped to the minimum permissions required for the declared permitted operations

**Connection Failure Behavior:**

Each declared connection must define what the agent does when the system is unavailable:

- For Read connections: connection failure behavior must align with the degraded-mode requirements in STD-TEC-AI-002 if the source is classified as Required in the Evidence Map
- For Write and Action connections: the agent must not silently retry or queue failed operations without notifying the user; connection failure must result in an explicit error state that the user can act on
page_texts.10:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Prefer User Delegated identity over Service Identity for Read connections — User Delegated identity preserves the user's own access model and reduces the governance burden on the agent
- Define retry policies for Read connections in the connection failure behavior to avoid unnecessary degraded-mode triggers from transient failures
- Review the System Connection Register at the same cadence as the Evidence Map — source owners, permissions, and connection endpoints change
page_texts.11:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Agents must not connect to any system not declared in the System Connection Register
- Credentials must not be stored in prompts, instructions, code, or unmanaged configuration files
- Service identities must not be granted permissions broader than the minimum required for the declared permitted operations
- Agents must not execute Write or Action operations without a human checkpoint unless automated execution has been explicitly approved per the requirements above
- Agents must not silently swallow connection failures for Write or Action operations
page_texts.12:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Exceptions to any requirement in this standard require written approval from the Data and Compliance Owner and the Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
2. Exception requests must specify the connection, the requirement being excepted, the business justification, the risk controls applied, and a remediation timeline
3. Approved exceptions are recorded in the capability registry with an expiry date and reviewed at the next governance cycle

page_texts.15:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#system-connection-register-completeness]

#### System Connection Register Completeness

- The System Connection Register must cover 100% of external system connections used by the agent
- Each entry must identify the system, classification, identity model, permitted operations, data sensitivity classification, system owner, connection failure behavior, execution mode (Write/Action connections), and credential rotation cadence (Service Identity connections)
- "External system" includes any system reached via API call, database query, connector, webhook, or any other integration mechanism — not only internet-facing systems
page_texts.16:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#service-identity-scoping]

#### Service Identity Scoping

- Service identity permissions must be scoped to the specific operations declared as permitted in the System Connection Register
- Broad permission grants (e.g., full read/write on a database, admin-level API access) are prohibited unless every permission in the grant corresponds to a declared permitted operation
- Service identity configuration must be reviewable — the permissions granted must be verifiable by the Data and Compliance Owner at governance gate review
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#human-checkpoint-implementation]

#### Human Checkpoint Implementation

- For agents requiring human checkpoints on Write or Action operations: the checkpoint must be implemented as an explicit confirmation step in the agent's interaction flow, not as a warning message that the user can ignore
- The checkpoint must present the specific operation to be executed — the system, the operation type, and the data or parameters involved — so the user can make an informed decision
- The agent must not execute the operation until confirmation is received; timeout or non-response must result in operation cancellation, not execution
page_texts.18:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#credential-storage]

#### Credential Storage

- Credentials used by agent connections must be stored in and retrieved from an approved enterprise secrets management service at runtime
- Hardcoded credentials in any artifact — prompt, code, configuration, infrastructure definition — are prohibited and constitute an immediate containment trigger
page_texts.19:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#architecture-constraints]

### Architecture Constraints

- An agent that uses a Service Identity for a connection must have that connection reviewed at a higher governance tier than a User Delegated connection — the Service Identity review is included in the capability contract governance gate
- Write and Action connections must be listed separately from Read connections in the System Connection Register; combined entries that obscure operation classification are not permitted
- Connection failure behavior for Write and Action connections must result in a user-visible error state — silent failure is not permitted for operations that change state in an external system

page_texts.22:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#phase-1-connection-discovery-and-declaration-before-pilot]

#### Phase 1: Connection Discovery and Declaration (Before Pilot)

1. Enumerate every external system the agent accesses or will access — including systems reached via platform connectors, custom code, API calls, and tool definitions
2. Classify each connection as Read, Write, or Action
3. Determine the appropriate identity model for each connection; document the business justification for any Service Identity selections
4. Document permitted operations for each connection with enough specificity to be verifiable
5. Confirm the system owner for each connection and obtain their acknowledgment that the agent's connection and permitted operations are appropriate
6. Complete the System Connection Register template
page_texts.23:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#phase-2-credential-and-access-configuration-before-pilot]

#### Phase 2: Credential and Access Configuration (Before Pilot)

1. Store all service credentials in the approved secrets management service
2. Configure service identities with minimum-scope permissions; verify that the granted permissions match only the declared permitted operations
3. Document the credential rotation cadence for each service credential in the System Connection Register
page_texts.24:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#phase-3-human-checkpoint-and-failure-behavior-implementation-before-pilot]

#### Phase 3: Human Checkpoint and Failure Behavior Implementation (Before Pilot)

1. For each Write or Action connection without approved autonomous execution: implement the human confirmation checkpoint in the agent's interaction flow
2. Test the checkpoint behavior for non-autonomous connections: verify that the agent does not execute without confirmation, and that non-response results in cancellation
3. For each Write or Action connection approved for autonomous execution: implement the audit logging required by condition 3 of the Human-in-the-Loop section; verify that every autonomous operation writes to the tamper-resistant log with all required fields
4. Implement connection failure behavior for each connection; test by simulating the target system being unavailable
5. For Read connections that are also Required sources in the Evidence Map: verify that connection failure triggers the correct degraded-mode behavior per STD-TEC-AI-002
page_texts.25:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#phase-4-ongoing-maintenance]

#### Phase 4: Ongoing Maintenance

1. Review the System Connection Register at each quarterly governance review — confirm system owners, permitted operations, and credential rotation status are current
2. When a new connection is added or an existing connection changes: update the System Connection Register and submit a change record per STD-GOV-AI-004 before the change takes effect in Production
page_texts.26:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| Connection declaration completeness | All external connections declared in the System Connection Register | Integration review comparing declared connections to agent configuration or code | System Connection Register |
| Classification accuracy | Every connection classified as Read, Write, or Action | Manual review of classification against actual operation behavior | System Connection Register |
| Identity model appropriateness | Service identities have documented justification and written approval from both the Data and Compliance Owner and the target-system technical owner | Approval record review | Approval record and System Connection Register |
| Service identity scoping | Granted permissions match declared permitted operations only | Permission configuration review by Data and Compliance Owner | Permission configuration evidence |
| Credential storage | No credentials in prompts, code, or unmanaged configuration | Code and configuration review | Code review record |
| Human checkpoint or audit log | Write and Action connections without approved autonomous execution have functioning human confirmation steps; connections with approved autonomous execution have audit logging per the Human-in-the-Loop section | Scenario testing — simulate write/action trigger and verify checkpoint or audit log fires | Test results |
| Connection failure behavior | Each connection has defined and tested failure behavior | Scenario testing with target system unavailable | Test results |
page_texts.27:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#documentation-requirements]

### Documentation Requirements

- System Connection Register: one entry per external connection; maintained by the agent owner; reviewed at each lifecycle promotion and quarterly
- Service Identity Approval Record: written approval from both the Data and Compliance Owner and the target-system technical owner for each Service Identity connection; archived in the capability registry
- Automated Execution Approval Record: written approval from Data and Compliance Owner for any Write or Action connection approved for automated execution without a human checkpoint

page_texts.30:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#assessment-criteria]

#### Assessment Criteria

- System Connection Register completeness: all connections declared, classified, and with system owner acknowledgment
- Credential management: no credentials stored outside the approved secrets management service
- Human checkpoint presence: all Write and Action connections without approved automated execution have functioning confirmation steps
- Service identity scoping: permissions bounded to declared permitted operations
page_texts.31:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#assessment-process]

#### Assessment Process

1. At Pilot promotion gate: Platform Governance Team reviews the System Connection Register for completeness; Data and Compliance Owner confirms service identity scoping and automated execution approvals
2. Monthly: Platform Governance Team verifies that no new connections have been added to Production without a corresponding System Connection Register update and change record
3. Quarterly: agent owner reviews the System Connection Register for currency — system owners, permissions, and credential rotation status
page_texts.32:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#non-compliance-handling]

### Non-Compliance Handling

- Undeclared connection discovered: immediate containment of the capability pending connection declaration and governance review
- Credential found outside secrets management: immediate containment; security incident process initiated
- Write or Action connection without human checkpoint and without approved automated execution: block promotion to Production; containment if already in Production
- Service identity with permissions broader than declared: remediation required before any lifecycle promotion
page_texts.33:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-008-ai-agent-system-connections.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
- **Compliance Manager**: Platform Governance Team (connection register completeness); Data and Compliance Owner (service identity and automated execution approvals)
- **Governance Body**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board (exception approvals)
- **Subject Matter Experts**: Security and Data Governance teams (credential management, service identity review)
